chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Al-ala' ibn Razin, from Umar ibn Yazid, from Imam Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever says in his Witr prayer, when he prays Witr: 'I seek forgiveness of God and I repent to Him' seventy times while standing, and persists in doing so until a year passes for him, God will record him among those who seek forgiveness at dawn, and forgiveness from God Almighty becomes obligatory for him.

key_terms.أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللَّهَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ: I seek forgiveness of God and I repent to Him
key_terms.بِالْأَسْحَارِ: At dawn / in the early morning hours

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting 'Astaghfirullah' seventy times in Witr prayer?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the transformative power of consistent dhikr by linking the Witr prayer's qunut to the Quranic virtue of 'al-mustaghfirin bi'l-asihar' (those who seek forgiveness at dawn). This practice not only secures divine forgiveness but also elevates the believer's spiritual status to that of the righteous who persist in repentance, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the interconnection between ritual prayer and daily spiritual discipline.
